 JUDGMENT

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows :
On 03-10-2023 at about 9.30 a.m., the petitioner was waiting for bus at road side,
near Belladamadu Gate, Sira- Madhugiri NH road, Kasaba Hobli, Madhugiri Taluk,
Tumakuru.
At that time, the rider of the two-wheeler bearing Reg. No.KA-64-V-8975 came very rashly and negligently, without caring for human safety and dashed against the petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner has fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Madhugiri Government Hospital and then shifted to Tumakuru Government Hospital and again shifted to Gurushree Hospital, Madhugiri, wherein he took treatment as an in-patient.
Earlier to the accident, he was student and was very active child and had a very good future.
Due to accidental injuries, he has suffered lot of physical and mental stress and frustration.
The Madhugiri Police have registered the case against the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-64-V-8975 for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 338 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% per annum.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondent No.1 has appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.
Whereas, the respondent No.2 did not choose to appear and remained absent.
Hence, the respondent No.2 is placed as ex-parte.
4. The respondent No.1 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It seeks protection under Section 147 and 149 of Motor Vehicle Act.
It is contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Sections 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.

Further it is contended that, the rider of the motorcycle was not holding valid and effective driving Ravi Teja vs Sbi General Ins Co Ltd on 1 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169600103/
2 licence to drive the same as on the date of accident.

sentences.text: The respondent No.2 being the owner of the motorcycle has contravened the provisions of Motor Vehicles Act and the rules framed there under and has committed the breach of the terms and conditions of the policy willfully, intentionally and consciously has entrusted the vehicle to a person who was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the insured vehicle, said to be involved in the alleged accident.

It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in favour of respondent No.2 in respect of motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-64-V-8975 and its validity as on the date of accident.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries sustained, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.
Further it is contended that, the motorcycle has neither involved in the accident nor it has caused any accident to the petitioner.
The guardian of minor petitioner in collusion with the jurisdictional police and the owner of the motorcycle has created false crime records and story of the accident, to get compensation.

In fact, as on the date of accident, the minor petitioner was negligent who without taking precautions, without having proper lookout over the oncoming vehicles along the road tried to cross the busy road, where there is no option to cross the road, due to which the petitioner fell down on the road and sustained injuries.
The accident occurred solely due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner himself.
ter lapse of several days, as such petition deserves to be dismissed for non-involvement of motorcycle.
Further, it has sought permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.2, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
Further it has contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 03-10-2023, at about 9.30 a.m., near Belladamadu Gate, Sira- Madhugiri NH road, Kasaba Hobli, Madhugiri Taluk, Tumakuru, due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-64-V- 8975 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3.
What order or Award ?

On the other hand, the respondent No.1 has examined the Record Keeper of Government Hospital, Madhugiri as R.W.1 and got marked 3 documents as Ex.R.1 to 3.

8. My findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 9. Issue No.1: It is specific case of the petitioner that, on 03-10-2023 at about 9.30 a.m., when the petitioner was waiting for the bus at road side, near Belladamadu Gate, Sira-Madhugiri NH road,
Kasaba Hobli, Madhugiri Taluk, Tumakuru, the rider of offending two-wheeler bearing Reg.
No.KA-64-V-8975 came in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner.
Due to said impact, the petitioner has fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Further it is contended that, earlier to the accident, he was student and was very active child and had a very good future.
Due to accidental injuries, he has suffered lot of physical and mental stress and frustration.
10. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has examined his father/natural guardian as P.W.1.
The P.W.1 has filed his examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein he has reiterated the entire averments made in the petition.
Further, in support of his oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked total 15 documents as Ex.P.1 to 15.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is true copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.2 is true copy of first information statement, Ex.P.3 is true copy of spot mahazer, Ex.P.4 is true copy of Motor Vehicle Accident report , Ex.P.5 is true copy of charge-sheet, Ex.P.6 is true copy of wound certificate,
Ex.P.7 and 8 are discharge summaries (total 2), Ex.P.9 are medical bills (total 20), Ex.P.10 are prescriptions (total 9), Ex.P.11 and 12 are notarized copy of Aadhar cards of minor petitioner and guardian, Ex.P.13 is case summary slip, Ex.P.14 is clinical notes and Ex.P.15 is x-ray.

11. On meticulously going through the above police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 6, prima-facia it reveals that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-64-V-8975 and dashing the same to the petitioner, who was pedestrian and waiting for the bus to board.
Further it reveals that, due to said impact the petitioner has fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries on his right leg.

The investigation officer in his final report, marked as Ex.P.5, has clearly stated that, the said accident is caused due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-64-V-8975 and dashing the same to the petitioner, who was waiting to board the bus and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries to his right leg in the said accident.

12. At the outset, it is pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.1 in respect of motorcycle bearing No.KA-64-V-8975 and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.

Further, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner has remained undisputed by the owner of offending vehicle/Respondent No.2, as she did not choose appear and contest the case of the petitioner.

Whereas, the respondent No.1 insurance company has specifically denied the above Ravi Teja vs Sbi General Ins Co Ltd on 1 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169600103/
4 averred facts and circumstances of the accident and taken specific defence that, the said accident has occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner himself and the motorcycle bearing No.KA-64-V-8975 was not at all involved in the alleged accident.

sentences.text: Further it is contended that, the guardian of the petitioner in collusion with the owner of motorcycle and jurisdictional Police has falsely implicated the said vehicle in the alleged accident and registered a false case against the rider of said vehicle, to have wrongful gain from the respondent No.1 insurance company.
But, the respondent No.1 has failed to establish the said contentions.
There is absolutely no corroborative oral or documentary evidence placed on record by respondent No.1 to show that, the said accident has taken place due to self negligence of the petitioner.
Further, there is no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondent No.1 to disprove the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-64-V-8975 and dashing the same to the petitioner, who was waiting for the bus on the road side and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries on his leg and other parts of the body in the said accident.

Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.1 has cross- examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence or which goes to show that, the said accident has taken place due to the negligence of the petitioner or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.

13. The Ex.P.3 spot mahazar also clearly speaks that, the accident has taken place on the left side of 20 feet wide Sira-Madhugiri NH road, near Belladamadu Gate, Kasaba Hobli, Madhugiri Taluk,
Tumakuru, due to dashing of offending motorcycle bearing No.KA-64-V-8975 to the petitioner, who was waiting for the bus on the road side.

Further, the Ex.R.1 MLC register extract also clearly speaks that, the patient was brought to the hospital with a history of road traffic accident at Belladamadu Gate, at 9:30 a.m., on 03-10-2023, he was pedestrian and hit by a two wheeler.
Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.4, the accident is not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle and there is no negligence on the part the petitioner,
then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of offending vehicle.
There is absolutely no material on record to show that, there was any contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner in the cause of accident.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-64-V-8975, the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
14. No doubt, there is a delay of 06 days in lodging the complaint by the petitioner.
But, the natural guardian of the petitioner/complainant in the Ex.P.2 first information statement has stated the reason for delay caused in lodging the complaint.
He has clearly stated that, as he was engaged in providing treatment to his son, there is a delay caused in lodging the complaint.
Further, it is settled proposition of law that, the delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt claimant's case in genuine cases.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Ravi V/s Badrinarayan and others,

sentences.text: In Indian conditions, it is not expected that a person would to rush to police station after accident.
The treatment of victim is given priority over lodging FIR.
The kith and kin of victim are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging FIR.

Hence, delay in lodging FIR not a ground to dismiss claim petition."
15.

There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents to disbelieve the reason for delay caused in lodging the complaint, stated in the Ex.P.2 first information statement of the complainant.

In such circumstances and in the light of ratio laid down in the above cited decision, this Court is of the opinion that, in the present facts and circumstances of the case, the delay for lodging the complaint is properly proved by the petitioner with cogent and satisfactory reasons.

16. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.6 wound certificate, Ex.P.7 and 8 discharge summaries (total 2), Ex.P.13 case summary slip, Ex.P.14 clinical notes and Ex.P.15 x-ray, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in a road traffic accident and he has suffered right distal fibula and distal tibia fracture.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

In such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that, the respondents have failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-64-V-8975 and the injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
17. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011) 11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

18. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, " in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."
19.

Tumakuru, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-64-V-8975.

sentences.text: Issue No.2:

While answering the above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident is caused due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-64-V-8975 and he has sustained grievous injuries.
As per the medical records placed on record by the petitioner, he has sustained right distal fibula and distal tibia fracture and for the said injuries he has undergone surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.
To prove his age, the petitioner has produced the notarised copy of his Aadhar card, which is marked as Ex.P.11.
As per Ex.P.11, the date of birth of the petitioner is 12-07-2011.
The accident has taken place on 03-10-2023 at about 9.30 A.M.
Therefore, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident was 12 years.
In the case in hand, petitioner is admittedly a minor of the age of 12 years as on the date of accident and he has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants,
transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.
21.

In the present facts and circumstances of the case, it is relevant to refer the decision of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, in the case of Master Karthik R. S/o V. Rajababu V/s National Insurance Co. Ltd., and another, reported in MFA No.426/2020 (MV-I) C/w MFA No.4124/2020 (MV-I) and MFA No.7008/2021 (MV-I), dated 27-09-2024.

entities.text: Master Karthik R. S/o V. Rajababu V/s National Insurance Co. Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the said decision, at Para No.25, the Hon'ble High Court has clearly held that:
"25.

In light of the fact that, the Apex Court has accepted that, the minor would suffer a pecuniary loss and has awarded compensation under this account in the case in Kajal's case and Ayush's case and it has held that, the minor should be awarded non- pecuniary loss for the injuries suffered in Master Mallikarjun's case, the ideal method for determining the compensation for minor would be to combine both the components i.e. compensation for the pecuniary loss (as determined in Kajal's and Ayush's cases) and also for the non-pecuniary loss (as determined in Master Mallikarjun 's case).

This methodology in determining the compensation would essentially take care of both the pecuniary and non pecuniary loss that a child would suffer as a result of a disability and would therefore constitute 'just compensation' as contemplated under the M.V. Act."
22.

In the light of above decision of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, the petitioner is entitled to compensation under the following heads:
i) Loss on future income: The petitioner has averred that due to accidental injuries,
he has sustained grievous injuries and he has suffered disability.

Further, the P.W.2,
who is the doctor, who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered right distal fibula and distal Ravi Teja vs Sbi General Ins Co Ltd on 1 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169600103/
7 tibia fracture and for the said injuries the petitioner has undergone surgery i.e. ORIF with plate and screws.

sentences.text: Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that, the petitioner has suffered permanent physical disability of 34% to the lower limb and 11.33% to the whole body.

The Ex.P.6 wound certificate, Ex.P.7 and 8 discharge summaries (total 2), Ex.P.13 case summary slip, Ex.P.14 clinical notes and Ex.P.15 x-ray are clear evident that, the petitioner has suffered the above mentioned injuries and he has undergone surgery for the said injuries.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.1 has cross-examined P.W.2 in length
, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
Further, he has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, there is no disability to him and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability to the petitioner.

But, it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.2 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 03-10-2023 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 22-01-2025, which is after lapse of one year and three months from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.
Further he has stated that, the petitioner requires one more surgery for removal of implants.
This clearly goes to show that, the disability has been assessed before completion of full treatment.
As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion of treatment.

sentences.text:
If the disability had been assessed after future surgery,
perhaps there would have been reduction in the percentage of the disability.

Further,
it is pertinent to note that, P.W.2 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, both the fractures are united and implants are in situ.
There is no fracture at hip and knee joint portion and the muscle power is normal.

Further he has clearly admitted hta,
there is every chances of early healing in case of tender age.

Therefore, considering the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 8% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 8% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
In the present case, the accident has taken place on 03-10-2023 at about 9.30 a.m.

As the accident has taken place in the year 2023, the notional income of the petitioner,
as indicated in the tabular column of Table-I, at Page No.25 Para No.44 of the judgment in Master Karthik R. S/o V. Rajababu V/s National Insurance Co. Ltd., and another, is considered at Rs.2,59,036/- per annum.

Rs.3,73,012/-.
ii) Food, nourishment and incidental charges:

As per Ex.P.7 and 8 discharge summaries (total 2), the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 4 days in District Hospital, Tumakuru and Gurushree Hospital,

iii) Medical expenses:
The petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.2,40,000/- towards medical, conveyance, food & nourishment, attendant charges and other incidental charge.
In order to prove the same, he has produced 20 medical bills, as per Ex.P.9.

iv) Conveyance expenses: The petitioner is the resident of D.V. Halli, Kasaba Hobli,
Madhugiri Taluk, Doddaveeragondanahalli, Tumakuru, the accident has taken place on Sira-Madhugiri NH road, near Belladamadu Gate, Kasaba Hobli, Madhugiri Taluk, Tumakuru and he has taken treatment at District Hospital, Tumakuru and Gurushree Hospital, Madhugiri.
Taking into consideration the distance in between the above places, compensation of Rs.5,000/- is awarded towards conveyance.

But, admittedly the P.W.2 has not issued estimation of cost for the said surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards future medical expenses would be just and reasonable.

In all, petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,83,109/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.
24. Liability:

Admittedly, as on the date of accident the respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-64- V-8975 and the insurance policy issued by the respondent No.1 in respect of said vehicle was valid from 29-05-2023 to 28-05-2028.
Further, there is no evidence on record to show that, there is any breach of terms and conditions of the said policy.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-64-V-8975 the accident has occurred and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.2 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.1 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.2.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.1 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,83,109/-,
with interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization, from the respondent No.1, I answer issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
25. Issue No.3:
In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:

opennyai_summary.facts: The Madhugiri Police have registered the case against the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-64-V-8975 for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 338 of I.P.C.
opennyai_summary.issue:
5. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.
Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 03-10-2023, at about 9.30 a.m., near Belladamadu Gate, Sira- Madhugiri NH road, Kasaba Hobli, Madhugiri Taluk, Tumakuru, due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-64-V- 8975 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3.
What order or Award ?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
When the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle and there is no negligence on the part the petitioner,
then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of offending vehicle.
There is absolutely no material on record to show that, there was any contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner in the cause of accident.
In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-64-V-8975, the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
But, the natural guardian of the petitioner/complainant in the Ex.P.2 first information statement has stated the reason for delay caused in lodging the complaint.
He has clearly stated that, as he was engaged in providing treatment to his son, there is a delay caused in lodging the complaint.
Further, it is settled proposition of law that, the delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt claimant's case in genuine cases.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Ravi V/s Badrinarayan and others,
Ravi Teja vs Sbi General Ins Co Ltd on 1 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169600103/
5 reported in (2011)4 SCC 693, has clearly held that, "the delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt claimant's case in genuine cases.
The kith and kin of victim are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging FIR.
Hence, delay in lodging FIR not a ground to dismiss claim petition."
15.
There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents to disbelieve the reason for delay caused in lodging the complaint, stated in the Ex.P.2 first information statement of the complainant.
In such circumstances and in the light of ratio laid down in the above cited decision, this Court is of the opinion that, in the present facts and circumstances of the case, the delay for lodging the complaint is properly proved by the petitioner with cogent and satisfactory reasons.
In such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that, the respondents have failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-64-V-8975 and the injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
17. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

6 20.
Therefore, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident was 12 years.
In the case in hand, petitioner is admittedly a minor of the age of 12 years as on the date of accident and he has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.
The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants,
transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.
21.
This clearly goes to show that, the disability has been assessed before completion of full treatment.
As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion of treatment.
If the disability had been assessed after future surgery,
perhaps there would have been reduction in the percentage of the disability.
There is no fracture at hip and knee joint portion and the muscle power is normal.
Therefore, considering the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 8% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 8% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
The respondent No.1 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.2.

With regard to the compensation for non-pecuniary loss, as the accident in the present case has taken place in the year 2023, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,67,173/-, as indicated in the tabular column of Table-II, at Page No.30 Para No.55 of the above judgment in Master Karthik R. with interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization, from the respondent No.1, I answer issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
